mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 2% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a potential overheating economy with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL is rising, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 3.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is consistently below 2% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.
